To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the protein content per newt embryo is low and constant throughout the development, and that the protein content of the cytoplasm and the nuclear protein soluble at pH 8.3 are synthesized at a low rate throughout the development.
the DNA content and protein content of Triturus pyrrhogastr embryos change during embryonic development.
the protein synthesis in the newt embryo during development is mainly confined to histones, and that qualitative changes of newly synthesized histone occur at gastrulation and late tail-bud stages.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following points: (1) the rate of synthesis and the amount of protein per embryo in each cell component; (2) the rate of protein synthesis per unit weight of cell components; (3) the rate of DNA increase in relation to the rate of protein accumulation; (4) the changes in the protein content and the rate and pattern of protein synthesis during development of the newt embryo.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
protein synthesis in the newt embryo is a complex process, which is controlled by many factors.
, except for yolk, the protein synthesis in Trituras embryos is active throughout development and that, at least for the nuclear protein, the synthesis is regulated by developmental changes.

the synthesis of protein is not uniform during the development of Triturus pyrrhogastrer embryos and that the synthesis of nuclear histone is the most active among the syntheses of protein in the embryo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the synthesis of nuclear histone was a continuous process during development, while that of the nuclear soluble protein and of the cytoplasm soluble protein were not.

the protein contents and the protein synthetic rates in the cytoplasm, yolk and nuclei were different in their development and that the nuclear protein was synthesized at the earliest stage and the rate of synthesis increased with development.
in Triturus pyrigogaster embryos, the synthesis of cytoplasmatic soluble protein is observed throughout development and that of nuclear protein at gastrula and late tail-bud stages.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the protein content of newt embryos decreases during development, and that the synthesis of cytoplasm soluble protein begins at the earliest stage studied, but that of yolk and nuclear proteins is delayed until later stages of development.
the newt embryo is an excellent model for the study of the development of protein in embryos.
it shows the potential to develop new, noninvasive methods for monitoring and quantifying protein expression in living cells.
